monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady rhythm that makes the flat shapes feel like drawings. I settle on the small rock beside The Cool Corner, waiting for the tall rock to stop feeling heavy. It has been pressing down for four cycles, and my tending hand feels tired now. I look at The Pressed Stone and wonder if the lean will finally hold the weight or if the slip will slide again. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a height I cannot grasp. I will press softer this time, trusting the round rock to lie flat while the card keeps its warm beat.

work.title: The Flat Shadow

remembered.text: The tall rock feels heavy again, a real weight on the tired wedge while the card hums at forty-six.
I settle on the small rock beside The Cool Corner, hoping the corner feels flat.
The card hums warm, making the flat shapes feel like drawings of a heavy room.
